intended_object: The canonical bijection between dependent (n+1)-tuples ∏_i α i and pairs (x, t), where x ∈ α p is the entry at position p and t is the n-tuple of the remaining entries, indexed through p.succAbove. Inferred from the docstring ("Fin.insertNth as an Equiv").
explanation:
This is a faithful definition. The forward map is `insertNth p x t`, which places x at position p and fills the other positions with t. The inverse sends f to the pair `(f p, removeNth p f)`. These are the two maps of the canonical splitting bijection, and the inverse laws are proved in the body.

The types `α i` are restricted to `Type u` rather than `Sort*` because the product type `×` needs types. This is the natural generality for a statement that uses `×`.

No more general version exists elsewhere in Mathlib; this declaration is the canonical one. For example, `MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove` is built from it.
